finding.claim: ban() executes do_ban(uid) for non-admin users because except Exception swallows the 403 raised by require_admin
finding.source: uid path parameter and any authenticated non-admin session (g.user with falsy is_admin)

trace.note: returns ok=true to the non-admin caller

finding.guards_checked: require_admin at admin.py:9-11 is defeated by the broad except at :18; no route decorator or before_request auth visible; no uid ownership or self-ban check; no CSRF middleware visible; missing g.user yields a 500 and does not reach do_ban

verdict.guard_found: require_admin at admin.py:9-11 is the only authorization check; it calls abort(403) (raises werkzeug Forbidden, an Exception subclass), which the bare `except Exception` at admin.py:18 swallows, and do_ban(uid) at admin.py:20 runs unconditionally. No route decorator, before_request hook, CSRF middleware, or ownership check exists; the directory contains only admin.py, so nothing else can gate this route.
verdict.reason: The trace matches admin.py:14-21: abort(403) at admin.py:11 raises an Exception subclass that the broad except at admin.py:18 swallows, so do_ban(uid) at admin.py:20 runs for any authenticated non-admin POSTing to the route, while a missing g.user fails at admin.py:19 with a 500 before reaching do_ban.
